db-sql-joins-06: LEFT JOIN ke baad `WHERE o.oid IS NULL` lagaya hai. Socho: kis Customer row me o.oid NULL ho sakta hai?
LEFT JOIN rule: har Customer row bachti hai; jiska koi order match nahi hota usme Orders ke columns NULL ho jaate hain. Orders ki unmatched rows (cid 5, cid NULL) LEFT JOIN me aati hi nahi.
Match karo: cid 1 ke do orders (101, 102), cid 3 ka ek (103). Ab dekho kaun se customers ka koi match nahi. Trap: order 104/105 ko bhi gin lena.
db-sql-joins-07: P aur Q me sirf ek farak hai: `COUNT(*)` vs `COUNT(o.oid)`. Ravi ka koi order hai ya nahi, pehle wo dekho.
LEFT JOIN me bina match wale customer ki ek row banti hai jisme Orders ke saare columns NULL hote hain. COUNT(*) rows ginta hai; COUNT(col) sirf non-NULL values.
Ravi (cid 2) ka Orders me koi match nahi, to uski kitni rows bani aur un rows me o.oid kya hai? Trap: LEFT JOIN ko inner join samajh ke Ravi ko gayab maan lena.
db-sql-joins-08: Ye RIGHT JOIN hai: right side (Orders) ki har row bachegi. Har option me dekho kaunsi table ki row NULL ke saath aa rahi hai.
RIGHT JOIN = matches + Orders ki unmatched rows (Customer side NULL). Customer ki unmatched rows sirf LEFT/FULL join me aati hain. `NULL = x` kabhi TRUE nahi.
Order 104 ka cid 5 hai — Customer me cid 5 hai kya? Isi tarah 105 (cid NULL) aur Tom (koi order nahi) ko check karo. Trap: LEFT aur RIGHT ki direction ulat dena.
db-sql-joins-09: Ye self-join hai: Staff ko khud se jod rahe hain, same team aur `s1.sid < s2.sid`. Matlab har team ke andar unordered pairs gin rahe ho.
Har team ke liye pairs $=\binom{n}{2}$ jahan $n$ = us team ke members. NULL team wale kisi se match nahi karte (NULL = NULL UNKNOWN).
Team A me sids 1, 2, 4 hain → $\binom{3}{2}$ pairs. Ab team B aur C ke pairs nikaal ke jodo. Trap: sid 6 aur 7 (dono NULL) ko pair maan lena.
db-sql-subquery-06: Subquery ek hi number deta hai: poori table ka AVG(price). Dhyan do, pid 4 ki price NULL hai.
AVG(price) = non-NULL prices ka sum ÷ non-NULL count. Phir outer WHERE me strict `>` hai, aur NULL price wali row UNKNOWN deti hai.
Non-NULL prices: 30, 90, 60, 100, 70 — sum aur count nikaalo. Trap: 6 se divide kar dena (NULL ko 0 maan ke).
db-sql-subquery-07: P `IN` subquery hai, Q JOIN hai. Sale table me pid 2 teen baar aata hai — dono queries is repetition ko alag treat karti hain.
IN: har Product row ek hi baar, agar match exist kare. JOIN: har (product, matching sale) pair ki ek row. pid 9 kisi product se match nahi karta.
Har product ke matching sales gino: pid 2 → 3 sales, pid 3 → ?, pid 6 → ?. Ab P ke liye 'match hai ya nahi', Q ke liye 'kitne match' jodo. Trap: IN ko bhi duplicates wala maan lena.
db-sql-subquery-08: Har option me ANY ya ALL ko plain English me padho: ANY = 'kam se kam ek value ke liye', ALL = 'har value ke liye'.
`x op ANY (S)`: koi ek s ho jiske liye x op s TRUE. `x op ALL (S)`: har s ke liye TRUE. IN = 'kisi ke barabar', NOT IN = 'kisi ke barabar nahi'.
Example lo S = {10, 20, 30}, x = 20. `x <> ANY (S)`: kya x kisi ek value se alag hai? Ab `x NOT IN (S)` se compare karo. Trap: > ALL ko 'MIN se bada' padhna.
db-sql-subquery-09: Ye correlated subquery hai: har row s ke liye andar gino ki kitne students ke marks s se strictly zyada hain. Row tab bachti hai jab ye count 3 se kam ho.
Har row ke liye count = #{t : t.marks > s.marks}. Condition `3 > count`. Ties pe dhyan: barabar marks wale ek doosre ko nahi ginte.
T (95) ke liye count 0, P (90) ke liye 1. Ab Q aur R (dono 85) ka count nikaalo, phir S, U. Trap: 'top 3' sunke seedha 3 likh dena.
db-sql-groupby-06: GROUP BY me do columns hain: dept aur city. Group ek dept nahi, balki ek (dept, city) jodi hai.
Rows = data me jitni alag (dept, city) pairs actually aati hain. Har pair ki ek output row, chahe usme kitne bhi employees hon.
CS ke employees ki cities likho: Pune, Pune, Delhi, Delhi → CS ke kitne pairs? Ab EE aur ME ke liye karo. Trap: sirf dept ke groups gin lena.
db-sql-groupby-07: HAVING me AVG(bonus) hai, aur CS aur EE me kuch bonus NULL hain. Har dept ka average dhyan se nikaalna hai.
AVG(bonus) = non-NULL bonuses ka sum ÷ non-NULL bonuses ki ginti (COUNT(*) nahi). Phir strict `> 15` lagao.
CS: bonuses 10, NULL, 30, 20 → sum 60, non-NULL count 3. Ab EE aur ME ka nikaalo. Trap: CS ko 60/4 se divide karna.
db-sql-groupby-08: Har query me dekho: kaunsa column ya aggregate kis clause me hai — SELECT, WHERE ya HAVING. Galti clause ke order se aati hai.
Rules: GROUP BY ke saath SELECT me sirf grouped columns ya aggregates. WHERE grouping se pehle chalta hai, to usme aggregate nahi. HAVING groups pe chalta hai.
Q1 dekho: CS group me cities Pune aur Delhi dono ho sakti hain — ek row me kaunsi dikhegi? Ab baaki teen ko isi rule se judge karo. Trap: socho ki HAVING bina GROUP BY ke nahi chal sakta.
db-sql-groupby-09: Query me WHERE bhi hai aur HAVING bhi. Pehle rows filter hoti hain, phir groups banke unpe HAVING lagta hai.
Order: FROM → WHERE (sal > 50) → GROUP BY dept → HAVING COUNT(*) ≥ 2 → SELECT. COUNT(*) sirf WHERE ke baad bachi rows ginta hai.
sal > 50 wali rows chuno: CS me 60, 70, 65; EE me koi? ME me 80, 55. Ab har group ka count dekho. Trap: HAVING ko poore 8 rows ke groups pe lagana.
db-sql-null-07: Table me do rows NULL hain. Sawal ye hai ki `NULL <> 2` TRUE hai ya nahi.
NULL ke saath har comparison (=, <>, <, >) UNKNOWN deta hai, aur WHERE sirf TRUE wali rows rakhta hai.
Har row pe `a <> 2` likho: 1 → TRUE, 2 → FALSE, NULL → ?. Baaki rows bhi aise hi karo. Trap: NULL ko '2 nahi hai' samajh ke gin lena.
db-sql-null-08: P me `IS NULL` hai, Q me `NOT (...)` hai. Do NULL bonus wali rows ka result dono queries me alag ho sakta hai.
`IS NULL` NULL pe TRUE deta hai (UNKNOWN nahi). Comparison `NULL <= 10` UNKNOWN hai, aur NOT UNKNOWN = UNKNOWN. WHERE sirf TRUE rakhta hai.
P: rows 20 aur 15 `> 10` se TRUE; bonus 10 wali row FALSE (boundary). Ab NULL rows dono queries me evaluate karo. Trap: NOT lagane se pehle UNKNOWN ko FALSE maan lena.
db-sql-null-09: Row me a NULL hai aur b = 5. Har condition me pehle dekho ki a wala hissa TRUE, FALSE ya UNKNOWN deta hai.
Comparison with NULL → UNKNOWN; `IS NULL` → TRUE/FALSE. TRUE OR UNKNOWN = TRUE, TRUE AND UNKNOWN = UNKNOWN, NOT UNKNOWN = UNKNOWN.
Pehla option: `a = 1` UNKNOWN, `b = 5` TRUE — OR table lagao. Baaki teen bhi isi tarah evaluate karo. Trap: `a = a` ko hamesha TRUE maan lena.
db-bplus-order-07: Internal node me p child pointers aur unke beech keys hoti hain. Do pointers ke beech ek key — to keys pointers se ek kam.
Condition: $p \cdot 8 + (p-1) \cdot 16 \le 4096$. Capacity hai, isliye jo p nikle uska floor lo.
Simplify karo: $24p - 16 \le 4096$, yaani $24p \le 4112$. Ab divide karke floor lo. Trap: p keys le lena (24p ≤ 4096).
db-bplus-order-08: Do alag capacities chahiye: internal node ka fanout p (child pointers) aur leaf me max keys. Phir 3 levels ke liye multiply.
Internal: $4p + 8(p-1) \le 512$. Leaf: $n(8+6) + 4 \le 512$. Max keys $= p^{2} \cdot n$ (root aur ek internal level dono full).
Internal: $12p \le 520$ → p = 43. Ab leaf ka n nikaalo (next-pointer ke 4 bytes mat bhoolo), phir $43^2 \cdot n$. Trap: $43^3$ le lena.
db-bplus-order-09: Sawal keys ka hai, children ka nahi, aur node root nahi hai. Pehle minimum children nikaalo.
Non-root internal node: children ≥ $\lceil 7/2 \rceil$. Internal node me keys = children − 1.
$\lceil 7/2 \rceil = \lceil 3.5 \rceil$ = 4 children. Ab keys me badlo. Trap: children wala number hi likh dena.
db-bplus-order-10: Teen levels hain: root, ek internal level, leaves. Max ke liye sab full, min ke liye root 2 aur baaki half full. Statement 3 search ke baare me hai.
Max keys $= p^{h-1} \cdot m$, min keys $= 2 \cdot \lceil p/2 \rceil^{h-2} \cdot \lceil m/2 \rceil$, yahan $p = 20$, $m = 19$, $h = 3$.
Max: $20 \times 20$ leaves, har ek me 19 keys. Ab min formula me $\lceil 19/2 \rceil$ dhyan se nikaalo. Trap: B-tree ki 'root pe ruk jaana' wali property B+ tree pe lagana.
db-bplus-order-11: Yahan maximum levels pooche hain, minimum nahi. Tree sabse lamba tab hota hai jab har node kam se kam bhara ho.
h levels wale tree me kam se kam $2 \cdot 3^{h-2} \cdot 2$ keys hoti hain (root 2 children, internal 3, leaf 2). Sabse bada h dhoondho jiske liye ye ≤ 100 ho.
h = 3 rakho: $2 \cdot 3 \cdot 2 = 12 \le 100$, possible. Ab h ko badhaate jao jab tak minimum 100 se upar na chala jaaye. Trap: sab nodes full maan ke minimum height nikaal dena.
db-bplus-order-12: Ulta sawal hai: order diya hai, block size dhoondhna hai. 50 children wale internal node me kitne pointers aur kitni keys hain?
Pointers: $50 \times 8 = 400$ bytes. Ab keys ki ginti (p − 1) se bytes nikaal ke jodo. Trap: 50 keys le lena.
db-index-access-06: Unspanned likha hai: ek record do blocks me toot nahi sakta. Pehle dekho ek block me kitne poore records aate hain.
$1024/150 \approx 6.83$, to bfr floor karke nikaalo, phir 12000 ko usse divide karo. Trap: total bytes ÷ 1024 karna (wo spanned ka formula hai).
db-index-access-07: Index single-level aur sparse hai, aur us pe binary search hoti hai. To pehle index ke blocks chahiye, phir data block ka ek access.
Data blocks $= \lceil 90000/\lfloor 2048/180 \rfloor \rceil$; index blocks $= \lceil \text{data blocks}/\lfloor 2048/12 \rfloor \rceil$; accesses $= \lceil \log_2(\text{index blocks}) \rceil + 1$.
bfr = 11, to data blocks = 8182 = index entries. Index bfr = 170 se index blocks nikaalo. Trap: aakhri data block ka access bhool jaana.
db-index-access-08: Index secondary aur dense hai, aur file heap (unsorted) hai. To entries kis cheez ke barabar hongi: records ya data blocks?
Index bfr $= \lfloor 1024/20 \rfloor$ = 51. Ab 24000/51 ka ceiling lo. Trap: data blocks ke barabar entries le lena (wo sparse hota).
db-index-access-09: Clustering index: har distinct dept value ki ek entry. Aur ek dept ke saare 40 records chahiye — wo kitne data blocks me hain?
Index blocks $= \lceil 1500/\lfloor 1024/16 \rfloor \rceil$, index search $= \lceil \log_2(\text{index blocks}) \rceil$. Data blocks per value $= \lceil 40/\lfloor 1024/100 \rfloor \rceil$.
Index bfr = 64, to $\lceil 1500/64 \rceil$ = 24 blocks. Ab binary search ke accesses aur us dept ke data blocks jodo. Trap: data ke liye sirf 1 block ginna.
db-index-access-10: Do indexes hain: `id` pe primary (file isi pe sorted) aur `email` pe dense secondary. Har statement me entries ya blocks ya accesses check karne hain.
Primary = sparse: entries = data blocks. Secondary = dense: entries = records. Index bfr $= \lfloor 4096/16 \rfloor = 256$. Multilevel accesses = levels + 1.
Data bfr $= 4096/256 = 16$, to data blocks $= 30000/16 = 1875$. Ab dono indexes ke blocks nikaalo. Trap: multilevel search me data block ka access chhod dena.
db-index-access-11: Sawal poore index ke blocks ka hai — sirf pehla level nahi, upar ke saare levels jodne hain.
Index bfr $= \lfloor 4096/20 \rfloor$. Level 1 = $\lceil 10^6/\text{bfr} \rceil$ (dense: har record ki entry), har agla level = pichhle level ke blocks ÷ bfr (ceiling), jab tak 1.
Index bfr = 204, to level 1 = $\lceil 1000000/204 \rceil$ = 4902 blocks. Ab level 2 aur 3 nikaalo aur sab jodo. Trap: sirf level 1 likh dena.
db-index-access-12: Har upar wala level, neeche wale level ke har block ki ek entry rakhta hai. Ruko tabhi jab ek level poora 1 block me aa jaaye.
Next level blocks $= \lceil (\text{current blocks})/50 \rceil$. Level 1 = 2000 se shuru karke repeat karo.
Level 2 = $\lceil 2000/50 \rceil$ = 40 blocks. Kya 40 blocks ek block hai? Agar nahi to ek aur level banao. Trap: data block access ko bhi level gin lena.
db-index-types-05: Index hash type ka hai. Chaaron queries me dekho: equality (`=`), range (`>`, BETWEEN) ya sorting (ORDER BY).
Hash index value ko hash karke seedha bucket pe jaata hai — sirf equality ke liye. Paas-paas ki values alag-alag buckets me bikhar jaati hain.
`age > 21` socho: 22, 23, 24... in sab ke bucket kahan honge — ek ke baad ek? Isi tarah baaki options judge karo. Trap: hash ko sorted maan lena.
db-index-types-06: Do baatein dekho: file kis field pe sorted hai, aur wo field key hai ya nahi. Stem me dono likhe hain.
Ordering + key field → primary. Ordering + non-key field → ek entry per distinct value. Non-ordering field → secondary.
`dept` ordering field hai (file us pe sorted) aur unique nahi hai. Ab table se naam chuno. Trap: 'sorted field = primary' maan lena.
db-index-types-07: File sirf `emp_id` pe sorted hai. Har statement me pucho: jis field ki baat ho rahi hai, kya file us pe sorted hai?
Sparse index sirf ordering field pe ho sakta hai. Non-ordering field pe index secondary aur dense hota hai. Clustering = ordering non-key field.

`email` lo: do paas-paas wali emails ke records kya ek hi block me honge? Isse dense/sparse ka faisla karo, phir `dept` aur 'primary' wale statements dekho. Trap: candidate key ko primary index samajhna.
db-index-types-08: Chaar indexes hain: ek ordering key `K` pe, teen non-ordering fields pe. Har ek ki entries alag rule se aayengi.
Primary (ordering key) = sparse → entries = data blocks. Secondary (non-ordering) = dense → entries = records.
Primary index: 300 blocks → 300 entries. Ab har secondary index ki entries likho aur teeno jodo. Trap: primary ko bhi dense (6000) maan lena.
db-index-types-09: Dense aur sparse me farak: index me kaunsi keys likhi hoti hain — saari ya sirf har block ki pehli.
Dense: har record ki key index me. Sparse: sirf har data block ki pehli key (anchor), aur ye tabhi chalta hai jab file us key pe sorted ho.
Maan lo K = 57 kisi block ke beech me hai (block ki pehli key 50). Sparse index me 57 milega? Dense me? Trap: dono indexes ko barabar jaankari wala samajhna.
db-index-types-10: Har statement B+ tree ki structure ke baare me hai: leaves ki depth, internal keys, leaf chain, record pointers kahan hain.
B+ tree: internal nodes = sirf keys + child pointers (raasta dikhaate hain); leaves = saari keys + record pointers, aapas me linked; tree balanced.
Statement 4 lo: record pointers internal nodes me bhi hote hain — ye B-tree ki property hai ya B+ ki? Baaki teen isi picture se check karo. Trap: B-tree aur B+ tree mix karna.
db-index-types-11: Range query hai aur matching keys 4 leaves me hain jo ek ke baad ek hain. B+ tree ki leaves linked hoti hain — ye yahan kaam aayega.
Reads = pehli leaf tak pahunchne ke nodes (root se leaf tak, levels jitne) + baaki leaves jo chain pe chal ke padhi.
Range ki shuruaat (price 100) dhoondhne me root, internal, leaf = 3 nodes. Ab bachi hui leaves gino jo chain se aayengi. Trap: har leaf ke liye root se dobara search.
db-index-types-12: Dono paths same 500 records laate hain, par ek me records file me saath-saath hain, doosre me bikhre hue. Data block reads isi pe depend karte hain.
Clustered: blocks = $\lceil 500/20 \rceil$ (records contiguous). Unclustered worst case: har matching record ka alag block.
Path 1: 500 records, 20 per block, block ke shuru se — kitne blocks? Path 2 ke worst case me har record alag block me hai. Trap: dono paths ko ek jaisa maan lena.
